question.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the following joint probability density function:

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{3x{y}^{2}}{14}, & \,0\le x\le 1,\,-1\le y\le 3 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Find the expression of the conditional probability density function ${f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x)$ for $0\le x\le 1,\,-1\le y\le 3.$
question.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the marginal density function for $X,$ we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(x) & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{3}\frac{3x{y}^{2}}{14}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{3x}{14}{\int }_{-1}^{3}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{3x}{14}\cdot \frac{{y}^{3}}{3}\,{|}_{-1}^{3} \\  & =\frac{x}{14}\cdot [27-(-1)] \\  & =2x.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the full expression for ${f}_{X}(x)$ is the following:

$$
{f}_{X}(x)=\{\begin{aligned}2x, & \,0\le x\le 1 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Now recall that the conditional probability density function of $Y$ given $X=x$ for two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given by

$$
{f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x)=\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{X}(x)},
$$

where

- $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability density function for $X$ and $Y,$ and

- ${f}_{X}(x)$ is the marginal density function for $X.$

Now, for $0\le x\le 1,\,-1\le y\le 3,$ we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x) & =\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{X}(x)} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{3x{y}^{2}}{14})}{2x} \\  & =\frac{3{y}^{2}}{28}.\end{aligned}
$$

For other values of $x$ and $y,$ the function $f(x,y)$ equals $0.$ As a result, ${f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x)$ will be equal to $0$ too.

Therefore, the conditional probability density function is the following:

$$
{f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{3{y}^{2}}{28}, & \,0\le x\le 1,\,-1\le y\le 3 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$
